Water Heating

Efficient water heating, sized for your home

Your water heater is one of the biggest energy users in the house. We help you compare tankless, heat pump and condensing tank-type systems, then install the one that fits how your household actually uses hot water.

Request a consultation (555) 010-0199
  • Lower water-heating energy use compared with older standard units
  • Options matched to your household size, fuel type and available space

Options

Water Heating options we offer

Heat pump water heaters

Move heat from the surrounding air into the tank instead of generating it directly, using far less electricity than a standard electric-resistance tank.

Tankless water heaters

Heat water on demand so there is no tank kept hot around the clock. A compact, wall-mounted unit frees up floor space.

Condensing tank-type heaters

Capture extra heat from exhaust gases for higher efficiency than a conventional gas tank, with a familiar storage setup.

Benefits

Why upgrade

  • Lower water-heating energy use compared with older standard units
  • Options matched to your household size, fuel type and available space
  • Guidance on electrical, venting and placement requirements before work begins
  • Help identifying incentive programs your upgrade may qualify for

Is it time?

Signs this upgrade could help

  • Your water heater is 10 or more years old
  • You run out of hot water or wait a long time for it
  • You notice rust, leaks or rumbling noises from the tank
  • You are planning an all-electric or energy-efficiency remodel

FAQ

Water Heating questions

Which is better: a tankless or a heat pump water heater?

It depends on your home. Heat pump water heaters suit homes going electric and need space with enough surrounding air, such as a garage. Tankless units suit homes with limited space and steady gas or electrical service. We walk through both during your consultation.

Will I need electrical work for a heat pump water heater?

Sometimes. Many heat pump water heaters need a dedicated circuit, and some homes need panel upgrades. We check this during the consultation so there are no surprises.

Are there rebates for upgrading my water heater?

Some programs offer incentives for qualifying water heater upgrades. Availability, amounts and eligibility change and are not guaranteed, so we review the current options with you before you commit.
